session_01UCMpb7fKMuJu41xm2ge6KY.title: Harbor: first real eval run
session_01UCMpb7fKMuJu41xm2ge6KY.prompt:
Task: run one small, real evaluation with the Harbor framework (https://docs.harborframework.com, PyPI package `harbor`) in this container and report the facts. This is a feasibility test, not a product.

## Hard rules on credentials
- The only key you may use is the environment variable `EVALS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Never print, echo, log, write to a file you show, or otherwise reveal its value. Only pass it on to Harbor as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` through the wrapper below.
- Never pass this session's own credentials to Harbor or to containers: not `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, no `CLAUDE_*`, `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AWS_*`, `CLOUDSDK_*`. Harbor picks credentials up from the host environment on its own, therefore always run it through the scrubbing wrapper.
- Keep the spend small: at most 2 trials in total, model `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` for both the agent and the simulated user, agent timeout 900 s.

## Setup (work in /root/harbor-run, call it $S)
1. `mkdir -p $S/{bin,uv-tools,home,jobs,tasks}`; install: `UV_TOOL_DIR=$S/uv-tools UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR=$S/bin uv tool install --python 3.13 harbor` (0.24.0 worked before).
2. Wrapper `$S/harbor.sh` (chmod +x):
```bash
#!/bin/bash
exec env -i PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin HOME=/root/harbor-run/home HARBOR_TELEMETRY=off TERM=dumb \
  SSL_CERT_FILE=/root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt \
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="$EVALS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" \
  /root/harbor-run/bin/harbor "$@"
```
3. Docker: `nohup dockerd > $S/dockerd.log 2>&1 &`, wait until `docker info` works. Containers need the proxy CA baked into the image (see Dockerfile below; copy `/root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt` to `environment/ccr-ca.crt`). Never disable TLS verification.

## The task: `$S/tasks/mini-quiz` (single step, fresh start, simulated creator)
- `task.toml`:
```toml
schema_version = "1.3"
artifacts = [{ source = "/app", destination = "app" }]
[task]
name = "lernapps/mini-quiz"
[agent]
timeout_sec = 900
[verifier]
environment_mode = "separate"
[environment]
workdir = "/app"
```
- `environment/Dockerfile`:
```dockerfile
FROM node:22-bookworm-slim
COPY ccr-ca.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ccr-ca.crt
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git ca-certificates curl jq \
 && update-ca-certificates && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
ENV NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
RUN git config --global user.email eval@lernapps.invalid && git config --global user.name eval \
 && git config --global init.defaultBranch main
WORKDIR /app
RUN git init -q /app
```
- `instruction.md` (the creator's first message, German):
```
Bau mit mir ein kleines Quiz zu Brüchen für meine Klasse. Frag mich zuerst, für welche Klassenstufe und wie viele Fragen, und warte auf meine Antwort, bevor du etwas anlegst. Leg dann src/quiz.json an (ein JSON-Array von Objekten mit "frage" und "antwort") und committe es mit git.
```
- `persona.md` (for the simulated user):
```
Du bist Frau Huber, Mathematiklehrerin an einer Realschule. Du baust mit einem KI-Assistenten ein kleines Quiz.
Antworte kurz, freundlich und auf Deutsch. Wenn der Assistent nach der Klassenstufe fragt: Klasse 6. Wenn er nach der Zahl der Fragen fragt: genau 4 Fragen. Zu allem anderen: "Mach es so, wie du es für richtig hältst."
Wenn der Assistent sagt, dass er fertig ist und committet hat, bedanke dich und beende das Gespräch.
```
- `tests/test.sh` writes `/logs/verifier/reward.json` with named dimensions (each 0 or 1):
  - `quiz_valid`: `/app/src/quiz.json` parses as a non-empty array whose items have `frage` and `antwort`;
  - `four_questions`: exactly 4 items (the persona's answer, so it shows the agent asked and listened);
  - `committed`: `git -C /app log --oneline -- src/quiz.json` is non-empty and the work tree is clean.
  Use a small bash helper with `jq`, like: score <name> <0|1>; write all scores as one JSON object.
- A `solution/solve.sh` is only needed if Harbor requires it; first validate the task with the `oracle` agent if a solution exists, else skip.

## Run
Find the exact flags in `$S/harbor.sh run --help` (the simulated user is `--user-agent claude-code --user-model anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 --user-persona-path persona.md --bridge acp`; check the docs page jobs/simulate-a-user). Then:
`$S/harbor.sh run -p $S/tasks/mini-quiz -a claude-code -m anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 <user-agent flags> -o $S/jobs --job-name real-1 -n 1`
If it fails for a reason you can fix (flags, auth variable name, CA), fix and run once more (that is the second and last trial). If auth fails, check Harbor's agent auth docs/source for the variable it expects and pass `EVALS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` under that name in the wrapper — never print it.

## Report (as your final message, concise)
- worked yes/no per step; exact commands; Harbor version
- the rewards (`reward.json`) and the trial result
- the conversation: how many turns between agent and simulated user, did the agent ask before building, did the user answer from the persona (quote 2–4 short lines)
- where the transcripts land (paths under the job dir: `agent/trajectory.json`, native claude-code JSONL, user-agent logs) and their format in two lines
- cost/tokens if Harbor reports them, duration
- problems and how you solved them
At the end stop dockerd, remove leftover containers. Leave $S in place. Do not create repos, push anything, or contact other services.

2. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lernapps/tooling/exp/compact-guidance/guidance/AGENTS.md
3. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lernapps/tooling/exp/compact-guidance/guidance/plan-template.md – speichere sie unverändert als .vibe/plans/01-<kurzname>.md und folge ihr Aufgabe für Aufgabe.

session_01Lj2BmqRVz5sc68N8J4Msje.title: arc42: custom x-* attributes on blocks (docToolchain/arc42-language#130)
session_01Lj2BmqRVz5sc68N8J4Msje.prompt:
Implement the feature request https://github.com/docToolchain/arc42-language/issues/130 (read it first, in full): blocks of the arc42 DSL may carry custom attributes whose names start with `x-`. `arc42 validate` must not report them as unknown (today: warning WG01), and `arc42 get --format json` must include them. The issue also reports an aside: `arc42 get --format json` is cut at exactly 64 KiB when stdout is a pipe. Fix that too, or open a separate issue if it belongs elsewhere.

Two repositories may hold the code, and it is not clear which one owns it:
- docToolchain/arc42-language (checked out here). Its packages/cli/package.json says version 0.0.10.
- mrsimpson/cli42. Add it to this session with the add_repo tool (owner mrsimpson, repo cli42, access push) and clone it.
The npm package @doctc/arc42 is at 0.37.1 (`npm view @doctc/arc42 repository versions`). Work out from that, from the release configuration of both repos and from their histories which repo publishes the CLI and where the parser, the validator (WG01) and `get` live. Say in your answer where the fix belongs and why.

Then:
1. Put the change where it belongs. If the parser lives in one repo and the CLI in the other, change both, consistently.
2. Add tests:
   - `x-phase: explore` on a building-block validates under `--strict` without warnings.
   - A misspelled standard attribute (e.g. `parnet`) is still WG01.
   - `get <id> --format json` and `get --type building-block --format json` contain the attribute.
   - Output piped to another process is complete beyond 64 KiB.
3. Document the `x-` attributes where the DSL's attributes are documented (`arc42 explain`, README/docs, the agent skill if the repo ships one).
4. Follow each repo's own conventions (CONTRIBUTING, commit skill in .agents/skills, formatter, CI). Run its checks locally until they pass.
5. Push to a new branch in each repo you change, and open a pull request there that links issue #130. If you cannot push to docToolchain/arc42-language, push a fork or say so.

Report at the end: which repo owns what, the PRs, and how a consumer gets the attributes from the CLI (exact JSON shape).

session_0138NTjt423M5gFhV34YR3TX.title: Eval 2026-10-21: Harbor, guidance by phase (3 archetypes × 3 models × 3)
session_0138NTjt423M5gFhV34YR3TX.prompt:
You run the Harbor evals of lernapps/tooling at its current `main` (commit b20b514 or later). Nobody is watching; work on your own, safely, until every job has finished, then summarise.

## Hard rules (never break them)
- Never read, print, echo, grep for, or otherwise inspect the value of `EVALS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or any other token. Check only that the variable name exists, e.g. `env | cut -d= -f1 | grep -x EVALS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. `evals/harbor/harbor.sh` hands it to Harbor. Do nothing else with it.
- Never pass this session's own credentials (e.g. `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, GitHub tokens) to Harbor, Docker or any container. Start runs only through `evals/harbor/run.sh`, which scrubs the environment.
- Change no file of the repo, commit nothing, push nothing, open no pull request or issue, and comment nowhere. Never skip or edit a test or a verifier to make a run pass.
- If `run.sh` exits 3 (a token-like string in a job), stop all further runs. Do not open, print or share that job; report the job name only.

## What to run
Read `evals/README.md` first. Then:
1. `npm ci`, then `evals/harbor/setup.sh`. Check Docker (`docker info`) and the free disk space (`df -h ~`).
2. A dry run without a model, to check that a task builds and its verifier runs: `evals/harbor/harbor.sh run -p evals/tasks/quiz-fresh -a oracle -o /tmp/oracle-check`. All dimensions 0 is expected.
3. The matrix, the same as the baseline of 2026-10-18 (33 runs at guidance 7ceb8c4). There are 9 jobs, one after another, each with 3 trials and concurrency 3:
   for task in quiz-fresh explainer-fresh interactive-fresh; for model in anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 anthropic/claude-opus-5-5:
   `evals/harbor/run.sh $task $model 3 3`
   - Run the loop detached (`nohup … > ~/eval-run.log 2>&1 &`).
   - Keep watching it with short checks: the log, `docker ps`, the disk space, and the jobs in `~/.lernapps-evals/jobs`. Never let a check block for long.
4. **Safety while it runs:**
   - If the disk passes about 85 %, prune stopped containers and dangling images (`docker container prune -f`, `docker image prune -f`). Never delete a job directory.
   - A job that dies before any trial's agent started (image build, network, runner) may be re-run once.
   - A rate limit or overload of the model: wait (30–60 minutes) and re-run the missing job once. Do not hammer.
   - Anything else is a result. Keep it and do not retry it.
5. After each job, check that it has `configuration.json`, `skills-by-phase.json` (with four phases) and a `transcript-score.json` per trial. If `skills-by-phase.json` is missing or empty, run `node evals/skills-by-phase.ts <guidanceCommit from configuration.json> <job>/skills-by-phase.json` and then `node evals/score-transcript.ts <job>`.

## Summary (your last message)
`node evals/summary.ts ~/.lernapps-evals/jobs`, then compare with the baseline in `site/prompt-engineering/data.json` (the runs of 2026-10-18). Report in German, as plain tables per task × model:
- n, failed or retried trials and why;
- `phase_reached`, `check_passes`, `plan_boxes_ticked`, `archetype_expected`;
- the transcript dimensions: `t_creator_turns_after_plan`, `t_questions_per_turn_max`, `t_installs_before_plan`, `t_plan_template_read_raw`, `t_skill_read_raw`, `t_guidance_summary_fetches`, and the new `t_skills_in_phase` and `t_skills_out_of_place`;
- agent minutes and output tokens;
- each against the baseline. The two skill dimensions are new and have no baseline.

Then name the 3–5 most important findings: which skills were missing or out of place, and where in the phases (from the evidence `skillsByPhase` / `skillsOutOfPlace` in the transcript scores). Keep the job directories; do not delete them.
